author: Juanita Adame
title: Fresno Unified classified workers raise concerns over stalled negotiations, possible layoffs - NewsBreak
text:
By Juanita Adame ,
3 hours ago
FRESNO, Calif. ( KSEE/KGPE ) – Classified employees with the Fresno Unified School District are speaking out, raising concerns about stalled contract negotiations and the possibility of layoffs as the next school year approaches.
Custodians, bus drivers, grounds crews and warehouse workers rallied Wednesday to bring public attention to what they say are growing concerns over the district’s budget and job security.
Andrew Martinez says workers feel little progress has been made at the bargaining table.
“And we don’t feel that there’s been any movement in the negotiation table,” Martinez said.
Martinez was one of several classified employees who spoke during the rally.
The group is represented by SEIU Local 521. He says workers previously addressed the school board, but have seen no meaningful changes since.
“We had gone and spoken to the board last month and tried to kind of not air grievances, but share our concerns,” Martinez said.
Workers say they fear classified employees would be among the first impacted if budget cuts are made, despite providing essential services across the district.
“So people like custodians, people like grounds workers and warehouse and bus drivers as well, all the people that are basically the infrastructure,” Martinez said.
Custodian Luis Munoz Soto also addressed the crowd, saying multiple departments could be affected if layoffs occur.
“Right now, all the departments are in danger, but the majority are gardeners, grounds, maintenance department, the custodians,” Munoz Soto said.
Munoz Soto added that if layoffs do happen, employees are asking for transparency and respect throughout the process.
“We don’t know exactly what will happen, but we are hearing this is what is predicted,” he said.
In response to the rally, Fresno Unified released a statement acknowledging the concerns and emphasizing ongoing negotiations with the union.
The statement read:
“The district and SEIU are meeting regularly to discuss these topics, as they are a top priority for Fresno Unified as well.
Because negotiations are underway, the discussions are confidential, but we can confidently state all positions receive a competitive salary and benefits package, and that safety is, and will always be, a priority.
Regarding staffing levels, due to declining enrollment, including reduced attendance following the COVID-19 pandemic, state funding tied to enrollment has decreased.
Reduced funding, combined with elevated staffing levels and program expenditures, have created the district’s current structural deficit and underscores the need for strategic budget realignment.
Fresno Unified is thoughtfully reviewing all possible options to continue sustainable quality education for students and evaluating resources and staffing across various employee classifications.
The district understands this information can be concerning and is committed to approaching any decisions with transparency and respect for district employees.”
